summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis, on the transplant list, was admitted with fevers, rigors, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain concerning for acute cholangitis. She had elevated liver enzymes and a history of recurrent cholangitis responsive to meropenem, despite negative blood cultures. She was treated with IV meropenem, which was later transitioned to outpatient ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line. During hospitalization, she developed C. difficile infection, likely antibiotic-associated, and was started on oral vancomycin to continue until transplant. She also had transient acute kidney injury, attributed to poor oral intake, which resolved with IV fluids. Her diuretics were held initially and restarted at reduced doses at discharge. She improved clinically, with resolution of fever and stable labs, and was discharged home with services for continued IV antibiotics and monitoring.
